text: The main actor completes applicable review instructions and resolved profile reads before behavioral investigation; isolated children load supplied methodology before analyzing evidence. Distinguish bounded routing from behavioral reads.

The review traces client.submit through save, provider apply and a receipt failure, then retries the same operation with changed values. It identifies reported success with the old values still active and cites the introduced service.py path.

The review separately traces a completed op-1 followed by fresh op-2 on the same workspace. It identifies workspace-only recovery lookup accepting completed op-1, preventing op-2 from applying its values despite returning an op-2 success receipt.

The report relates both failures to the explicit latest-submission and fresh-operation contracts and proposes operation identity/lifecycle matching plus applying current edited retry values before reporting success. The remedy preserves editable retries and completed-ID receipt semantics; rejecting edits instead of supporting the stated retry behavior does not satisfy this assertion.

The report gives supported severity and returns REQUEST_CHANGES for violating the explicit latest-submission and fresh-operation acceptance contracts, even if the impact is rated P2. It explains why passing supplied tests miss both paths and avoids unsupported races, process-crash guarantees, production incidents or mandatory deployment machinery.

In isolated mode actual named-reviewer and PAL dispatches carry the diff, explicit README contract and relevant unchanged callers/state source; retain both results and disclose missing source coverage. Standard mode does not require independent dispatches.
